comparisons.peer_topic: Derivative Instrument Presentation and Netting Adjustments
comparisons.peer_summary: The table presents derivative assets and liabilities on a gross basis prior to netting, which are then adjusted to reflect counterparty and cash collateral netting effects from legally enforceable master netting agreements.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC disclose tables for derivative instruments that explicitly address the impact of counterparty netting and cash collateral on fair value measurements. GS states that 'Counterparty and cash collateral netting represents the impact on derivatives of netting across levels' and presents financial assets and liabilities carried at fair value. Similarly, BAC presents derivative instruments on a gross basis which are then 'adjusted on an aggregate basis to take into consideration the effects of legally enforceable master netting agreements, which include reducing the balance for counterparty netting and cash collateral received or paid.' Both disclosures focus on how legal agreements affect the reported fair value of derivatives, though BAC explicitly details the gross-to-net adjustment mechanism.

sentences.text: The table below presents financial assets and liabilities carried at fair value.
• Counterparty and cash collateral netting represents the impact on derivatives of netting across levels.
Balances are presented on a gross basis, prior to the application of counterparty and cash collateral netting.

Total gross derivative assets and liabilities are adjusted on an aggregate basis to take into consideration the effects of legally enforceable master netting agreements, which include reducing the balance for counterparty netting and cash collateral received or paid.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fair value percentage calculation methodology excluding cash collateral
comparisons.peer_summary: Percentages in the fair value tables are calculated based on total assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis, excluding cash collateral paid or received on derivatives, because the cash collateral amounts have not been allocated to Level 1, 2, and 3 subtotals.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and C provide methodological details on how cash collateral impacts the presentation of fair value hierarchy tables. GS notes that 'Counterparty and cash collateral netting represents the impact on derivatives of netting across levels,' implying collateral affects the level classification or netting. C explicitly states that because 'cash collateral paid/received has not been allocated to the Level 1, 2 and 3 subtotals,' percentages are calculated excluding such collateral. Both disclosures highlight the specific treatment of cash collateral in the context of fair value hierarchy reporting.
